messages:
anita: Quick sanity check — onboarding Quill-v2 (int4) embeddings. Running recall@10 on our short-query holdout and seeing a consistent ~6% drop vs fp16 baseline. anyone else hit this? :thinking_face:

mike: saw a tiny dip on longer tails but not that big for short queries. can you paste the eval command you ran?

anita: ran the usual script: `./eval/recall.sh --model quill-v2-int4 --holdout short-queries --k 10 --metric recall`

anita: embed-eval-bot posted results right after:```
embed-eval-bot: model=quill-v2-int4 holdout=short-queries recall@10=0.726 baseline=0.789 delta=-0.063
```

sara: interesting — did you normalize embeddings before nearest-neighbor? int4 quant can change scale. are you using cosine or dot?

anita: cosine. I do `normalize=True` in the pipeline. code:```python
vecs = model.embed(batch)
vecs = vecs / np.linalg.norm(vecs, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```

rob: two quick things to try: 1) check per-channel vs per-tensor int4; 2) try whitening/centering before normalization. quantized weights can shift mean.

mike: also check batchsize during embedding — we saw different activation-order rounding effects when batchsize>32. which batch size did you use?

anita: default 64. i'll rerun at 8 and 1.

ops-bot: FYI pushed an earlier dedicated runtime patch yesterday that adjusted the kernel reorder for int4 GEMM — could affect results if you're on that cluster.

sara: can you run a quick kmeans cluster-coherence check? if clusters for short queries smear into nearby classes that's telling. try silhouette score and inspect nearest neighbor distances.

anita: running `python tools/cluster_check.py --model quill-v2-int4 --kmeans 128 --metric cosine` now. will post numbers.

embed-eval-bot: quick pass: silhouette_mean=0.19 (int4) baseline_fp16=0.26; avg_nn_distance_shortq=0.48 vs baseline=0.41

mike: okay silhouette drop suggests quantization noise increases intra-cluster distance. next test: run per-channel int4 quant (if supported) or try 6-bit. also run L2 instead of cosine as a sanity check.

rob: another check — are you applying the same post-processing (PCA/whiten) used in production? onboarding harness sometimes forgets the production projection which reduces recall.

anita: good call — onboarding harness does not include the 256-d PCA we use in production. I re-ran with PCA and preliminary recall@10 is back to 0.78 for int4.

mike: aha. so delta was mostly from missing production projection pipeline + quantization scaling. still good to assess pure quant effect though.

sara: please create a tiny ablation matrix: [no-pca, pca], [per-tensor, per-channel], [bs=1,8,64], [cosine,dot]. we can grid it quickly on a single node.

anita: will do. scheduling a short run now on node-ml-12 (low-priority). ETA ~ 12m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
